- The amide C(=O)N can be disconnected to give a carboxylic acid/derivative and an amine

- Benzothiazole core with cyano at position 2
- At position 7 (or other), there's NH-C(=S)-NH-C(=O)-Ph

1. A benzothiazole amine + phenylisothiocyanate (for the thiourea part)
2. Or the reverse - the amine on the phenyl side + isothiocyanate on the benzothiazole side

The thiourea linkage connects the benzothiazole nitrogen to the phenyl carbonyl through a sulfur atom. The exact precursor depends on which nitrogen bears the carbonyl versus the sulfur in the final structure. I need to reconsider the connectivity here. So the structure is actually a benzothiazole-2-carbonitrile with a 7-amino group connected via thiourea to phenyl.

For the retrosynthesis, I should disconnect the thiourea bond to reveal the two starting materials: the benzothiazole amine and phenyl isothiocyanate. The benzothiazole precursor would be 2-cyano-7-aminobenzothiazole, and the other fragment is simply phenyl isothiocyanate. I'm trying to work backwards from the product structure to identify the starting materials. The thiourea linkage suggests a reaction between an amine and an isothiocyanate. If I disconnect at the C-S bond, I'd get either a benzothiazole amine with phenyl isothiocyanate, or a phenyl amine with a benzothiazole isothiocyanate. The second option seems less likely since isothiocyanates are typically derived from primary amines rather than heterocyclic systems. So the most probable precursors are the benzothiazole amine and phenyl isothiocyanate. I need to verify the numbering of the benzothiazole ring system. The sulfur is at position 1, nitrogen at position 3, so the carbon between them is position 2.
